summary: Jake H. Davis is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Marlboro College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and CUNY, his posts include Brown University, the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies, and New York University.
Jakob Bucher worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission and was appointed superintendent at the Anglo-Vernacular High School in 1890.
Jakob H. Thiessen, born in 1854, specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Kiel University between 1875 and 1880 under the supervision of Richard Pischel.

Jakob Halfmann works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held the Chair of Comparative Philology at the University of Würzburg (2023–2025) and became a group leader at the Free University of Berlin in 2026.

Jakob Hausheer (1865–1943) studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler and Adolf Kaegi, and earned his Ph.D. at Halle-Wittenberg. In 1905, he became ordinary professor for Old Testament studies and Oriental languages at the University of Zurich.

Jakob Steiner (1796–1863) studied at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Beuth Hochschule für Technik Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Basel, Oxford, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe, he served as professor of Indology at Marburg (1925–1927) and held a chair at Tübingen (1927–1945).
Jakub Čejka is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He completed both an MA (1990–1998) and a BA (2018) at Charles University.

James A. Benn specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he held teaching posts at Lewis & Clark College and McMaster University.

James A. Santucci works in religious studies and Indology. He has served as professor of religion at California State University and as chair and professor of comparative religion at California State University, Fullerton.
James Adam (1860–1907) was a scholar of philosophy. He completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen from around 1876 to 1880 and at Gonville and Caius College from around 1880 to 1884.

James Alan Matisoff (born 1937) is a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist. He earned degrees from Harvard and UC Berkeley, taught at Columbia University (1966–1969), and became professor emeritus at UC Berkeley after serving from 1970 to 2002.

James Atkinson (1780–1852) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies who attended the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Indian Medical Service, Fort William College, and the India Government Mint in Kolkata.

James B. Apple specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of John D. Dunne, having also studied under numerous traditional and academic teachers.

James Bird (1797–1864) studied at Aberdeen and Guy's and St Thomas'. He worked in Indology and history/archaeology, serving as an assistant surgeon in Bombay, secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and vice-president of The Asiatic Society.

James Bissett Pratt (1875–1944) studied at Williams College and Harvard under William James. A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he taught at Visva-Bharati University and was a long-serving philosophy professor at Williams College.

James Blumenthal (1967–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.
James Bradstreet Greenough (1833–1901) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his A.B. at Harvard University in 1856 and subsequently served there as tutor of Latin from 1865 to 1873.

James Burgess (1832–1916) worked in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Glasgow and Edinburgh, he taught mathematics at Doveton College and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1886 to 1889.

James Burnell Robinson (born 1944) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and served as associate professor of religious studies at the University of Northern Iowa.
